title: X-Strata separates aneurysm sacs and overlapping vessels in two-view angiography
summary: X-Strata uses learned decomposition of cine angiography and parallax between two views to infer aneurysm-sac and vessel layers and reconstruct a 3D sac surface. On 220 held-out patients from three centers, including 122 external cases, the method ranked first among 14 baselines for sac recovery in overlap regions and layer ordering. All evaluated patients had same-session 3D rotational angiography as reference; performance and clinical benefit for patients with only 2D angiography remain unestablished.
ai_technology: A neural network estimates angiographic layers and contrast curves; a second view supplies depth-order cues for 3D reconstruction.
organization: Tsinghua University; Hunan University; Chinese PLA General Hospital; Air Force Medical Center of the Chinese PLA

evidence.tested: Held-out patient evaluation across three centers compared two-view X-Strata with 14 baselines and same-session 3D rotational angiography references.
evidence.unknown: The evaluated cohort had 3D rotational angiography; use in patients with only 2D imaging and any clinical-outcome benefit require separate evaluation.
